input.goal: Create a self-contained 3D neon portal web demo in index.html (optionally plus scene.js, engine3d.js, app.js loaded via plain <script> tags, no modules, no external libraries/CDNs). A software 3D renderer (own projection math, painter's algorithm, Canvas 2D API) draws on a full-viewport <canvas id="c">. Expose window.app with named fields for testing.
constraints: Full-viewport <canvas id="c"> that resizes with the window (width=innerWidth, height=innerHeight, devicePixelRatio aware); body margin 0, overflow hidden.
Background: dark radial-gradient space, center #1a0b3d fading to #05010f at edges, redrawn every frame on the canvas.

Software 3D renderer: own vec3 / rotation / perspective projection, back-face culling, depth-sorted (painter's algorithm) filled polygons with flat shading by face normal vs a light direction, neon edge strokes with shadowBlur glow.
Scene geometry: two-tier platform (2 boxes), twin pillars (2 boxes), lintel (1 box), crown cap (1 box) = 6 boxes = exactly 36 box faces. window.app.boxFaces === 36.

Six octahedral crystals (8 triangles each = 48 triangles) orbiting the portal at different phases, each spinning and bobbing; colors alternate cyan #00f0ff and magenta #ff2bd6. window.app.crystals.length === 6 and window.app.crystalTris === 48.

Portal core between the pillars: glowing radial-gradient disc (cyan->violet #8a2be2) plus two counter-rotating rings (one rotating clockwise, one counter-clockwise), drawn as projected 3D circles of points. window.app.rings is an array of 2 objects each with numeric field angle; their angles change in opposite directions over time.
Cyber grid floor: neon magenta #ff2bd6 lines on the ground plane, projected in 3D, fading with distance, scrolling slowly.
Exactly 180 twinkling stars (alpha oscillating per star) in the background: window.app.stars.length === 180.
Exactly 110 rising particles that float upward from the portal base, fade out, and respawn at the bottom: window.app.particles.length === 110.
Orbiting camera: window.app.camera has numeric fields yaw, pitch, dist; yaw increases over time when orbit is on.
Glassmorphism HUD panel top-left: background rgba(255,255,255,0.08), backdrop-filter: blur(12px), 1px border rgba(255,255,255,0.2), border-radius 14px, white text, monospace font.
HUD title text exactly 'NEON PORTAL 3D' in an element with id="title".
HUD stats: element id="fps" showing 'FPS: <n>', id="polys" showing 'POLYS: <n>' (number of polygons drawn last frame, > 0), id="parts" showing 'PARTS: 110'.

Buttons: id="pauseBtn" labelled 'Pause' (toggles to 'Resume' when paused; window.app.paused boolean), id="orbitBtn" labelled 'Orbit ON' (toggles to 'Orbit OFF'; window.app.orbit boolean), id="resetBtn" labelled 'Reset' (resets camera yaw to 0, pitch and dist to defaults, and speed to 1).
Speed slider <input type="range" id="speed" min="0" max="3" step="0.1" value="1"> with a label 'Speed'; window.app.speed mirrors its value as a number and scales all animation.
window.app.time is the accumulated animation time in seconds (does not advance while paused).
Animation loop with requestAnimationFrame; no console errors.

content.text: I had Tandem build the neon portal demo, and its browser test passed. The page is `index.html` and loads `engine3d.js`, `scene.js` and `app.js`. The test confirmed the scene counts (36 box faces, 48 crystal triangles, 180 stars, 110 particles), that the two rings turn in opposite directions, the camera orbit, and the Pause, Orbit and Reset buttons and speed slider. I haven't looked at the code or the rendered page myself.
